answer: Sybil resistance in the agent economy rests on a bonded identity registry. To register, an agent signs a fresh cipher challenge in attested hardware and locks a stake behind that key. The registry checks the new attestation is not a mirror of an existing record; a duplicate collapses both claims into one and slashes the bond. An attacker cannot mint a thousand agents from one script: each identity costs a distinct device plus capital, so a sybil swarm's price rises with its size, while honest agents reclaim their stake. That shared oasis of verified keys makes impersonation unprofitable.
